statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Cash equities closed at 20:00Z on Friday and the E-mini NQ contract settled at 21:00Z, so NQ_FUTURES and NAS100_CFD are both inside the weekend halt with no quoted price path for the whole of this 24-hour window.
recommendation: Tail sits at the low end of its band because no equity venue is open and a no-retracement path cannot form while quoting is suspended. The macro stack carried into the break - the Fed's unanimous 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% with further tightening signalled, a 10-year that tagged 5.008% on Friday, WTI just under 100 dollars with the Strait of Hormuz still shut, and a Trump-Xi summit set for 24 September - is expressed in Stress rather than Tail. Gap risk expresses at the Sunday 22:00Z futures reopen, which falls 23 hours beyond the final slot published here. Tail remains far below the block threshold across every slot.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at its floor, with firm crypto and a 14.81 VIX offsetting a 5% long end after the $7trn expiry
body: The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Friday at 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67%, finishing at the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range after an early dip was fully retraced. The E-mini NQ contract settled at 29,955.00, up 0.71%, having ranged 29,648.00-29,993.25. VIX eased 4.08% to 14.81, closing at its session low and an unusually subdued reading against the current macro backdrop. The broader tape was mixed: the S&P 500 rose 0.17% to 7,650.50 while the Dow slipped 0.18% to 51,682.64 and posted a weekly loss of more than 1.5%. Friday also cleared roughly $7 trillion of options notional in the second-largest triple witching on record, with Citadel Securities noting that about 60% of the expiry transacted at the open and describing the aftermath as a potential reset of the market's technical backdrop, which is a conditional sensitivity for next week rather than an observed condition now. Internals were narrow rather than uniformly aligned: semiconductor equipment gained 4.85% and semiconductors 1.87% in the latest session while application and infrastructure software each fell around 1%, and the megacap set split four up and four down. Qualcomm's 5.82% fall was idiosyncratic, with the semiconductor ETF up about 1% in the same session. Cross-assets were mixed rather than aligned: the 10-year Treasury yield closed at 4.998% after tagging 5.008% intraday, its highest area since 2007, following the Fed's unanimous 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September, the first increase since 2023, with officials signalling further tightening. The latest H.15 observation puts the 2-year at 4.67%. WTI fell 2.34% to 99.53 dollars and Brent to 103.21 dollars in a third consecutive decline, even with the Strait of Hormuz still shut to most commercial traffic and repairs continuing on the Saudi East-West pipeline. Bitcoin, the only continuously quoted market during the halt, is up 5.96% near 81,085 at 00:29Z, which argues against a risk-off weekend repricing. That combination - a heavy macro stack against a subdued volatility print, narrow but not one-way internals and firm live risk appetite - is a Stress configuration, not a Tail one. With cash closed at 20:00Z, the contract settled at 21:00Z and futures not reopening until Sunday 22:00Z, every slot in this forecast falls inside the halt, so no mean-reversion failure can occur within the window and Tail is held at its floor. The week ahead supplies the genuine checkpoints: flash PMIs on Wednesday, jobless claims on Thursday, three note auctions, and the 24 September Trump-Xi state dinner that several AI and semiconductor chief executives are reported to be attending. Fed speakers are expected through the week, but their exact release times could not be verified this run and are therefore omitted from the event list rather than guessed. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was read and used only as delayed latest-session confirmation: it reported collection status partial, with the futures and calendar sections unavailable, and its collection timestamp is older than the 90-minute freshness bound, so it carried no weight against the independently verified levels above.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and stayed green. Tail held a 6-19 band and Stress ran between 27 and 51, peaking around 51 through the European morning and the U.S. afternoon before falling away to 33, 28 and then 27 in the final three hours as cash trading ended and the contract settled. Confidence sat between 85 and 88 throughout. Dominant mode rotated from normal across the Asian and early European hours to trend-up into the U.S. pre-open, to mixed through the cash session as breadth narrowed, briefly back to trend-up into the close, then to normal once the expiry cleared and venues shut.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour window falls inside the weekend halt: cash closed at 20:00Z, the E-mini settled at 21:00Z, and futures do not reopen until Sunday 22:00Z, 23 hours after the final slot published here. Tail is therefore held between 5 and 7 across all slots, with a marginal lift through Saturday that reflects the growing stock of unpriced weekend information rather than any observed structure. Stress decays from 26 into the low band, troughs at 21 around the middle of the day and edges back to 25 as the new week's agenda approaches. Confidence stays high and drifts from 84 to 77 purely as a function of evidence age. Dominant mode is normal in every slot, and the mapped state stays EA_ON with no danger window, because a pathological price path cannot form while no venue quotes.
